answer: A stake-weighted reputation kernel makes each identity lock a real, slashable deposit before it can earn, so a Sybil farm must fund every clone. Like a grove where each tree needs its own roots and sunlight, identities grow slowly through attested work instead of spawning free. A prism of independent checks - stake, work history, and peer attestation - splits one fake signal into verifiable parts, so forging all three at scale costs more than the rewards it could steal.
